findings.evidence: FieldRange.lean:69-71 is `Module.Finite.of_equiv_equiv f.equivFieldRange.toRingEquiv.symm (RingEquiv.refl L) <| by ext z; simpa [h] using …`; mathlib/Mathlib/RingTheory/Finiteness/Basic.lean:376-380 shows `of_equiv_equiv (e₁ : A₁ ≃+* A₂) (e₂ : B₁ ≃+* B₂) (he …) [Module.Finite A₁ B₁] : Module.Finite A₂ B₂` — a pure transport, with the tower internal to Mathlib's proof, not to this one.
findings.fix: Rewrite the first paragraph to describe the actual argument — transport of `Module.Finite` along the ring equivalence `f.equivFieldRange` with the identity on `L`, the commuting square supplied by `h` — mirroring the comment already on `finrank_fieldRange` (lines 49-50), which uses the same technique.
findings.issue: The docstring of `finiteDimensional_of_fieldRange` states a proof that is not the proof: "The range restriction `f.equivFieldRange` is onto, so `f.fieldRange` is finite over `K`, and the tower `K → f.fieldRange → L` carries finiteness the rest of the way." The body builds no `Algebra K f.fieldRange`, no `IsScalarTower`, and no intermediate finiteness — it is one application of `Module.Finite.of_equiv_equiv` transporting along `f.equivFieldRange.symm`.

summary: The instance-plumbing plus scalar-tower derivation for a composite isogeny is now written out verbatim in three proofs (degree_comp, separableDegree_comp, inseparableDegree_comp), hiding a reusable fact; and the new finiteDimensional_of_fieldRange docstring explains a tower argument its proof does not use.
